# Requirements Document: Ancillaries and the flights they depend on

## Introduction

A bag, a seat or a meal is a service of its own in the order, for one
passenger on one flight segment, and it depends on the flight service for that
passenger and segment.  The guide records the link in two ways.  The page on
impacted dependent services shows a dependent service naming its parent
flight service by reference; the worked examples for adding an ancillary link
bags and seats to the flight only through the shared passenger and segment.
The model takes the link as a parameter, a reading of the sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Ancillaries/Basic.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-601

**User Story:** As an airline, I want to know which bags, seats and meals depend on a flight, so that a change to the flight reaches every service it affects.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL count as dependent on a flight service the ancillary services of the order that the link between dependent and parent ties to it. (Lean: `dependents`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHERE the order links a dependent service to its parent by reference THE SYSTEM SHALL count an ancillary service of the order as dependent on a flight service exactly when it names that flight service as its parent.
   - ONE-601.1, proven: proven theorem `dependents_by_reference`; example `seatWithoutReference`
2. WHERE the order links a dependent service to its parent through passenger and segment THE SYSTEM SHALL count an ancillary service of the order as dependent on a flight service exactly when it is for the same passenger on the same segment.
   - ONE-601.2, proven: proven theorem `dependents_by_passenger_segment`; example `seatWithoutReference`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL count no flight service as a dependent.
   - ONE-601.3, proven: proven theorem `dependent_not_flight`; example `seatWithoutReference`
4. WHEN an order holds an ancillary service and a flight service for the same passenger and segment THE SYSTEM SHALL count the ancillary service as dependent on that flight service.
   - ONE-601.4, open: open theorem `dependents_cover`; counterexample `seatWithoutReference`

#### Open question on ONE-601.4

> An ancillary for the same passenger and segment as a flight service of the
> order is counted as dependent on it, under either reading.
>
> Open question for the business.  Under the reference reading only an
> ancillary that names its flight counts.  In the seat worked example the seat
> services name no flight service, so a seat for the passenger on the flight is
> not a dependent of it, and a change to the flight reports no impact on the
> seat.  The example `seatWithoutReference` shows it.  Which link defines
> the dependency: a reference to the parent, or the shared passenger and
> segment?  And may an ancillary depend on another ancillary, such as a lounge
> pass on a premium seat?
